payload.claim: The comment at ledger.py:164-166 claims RUN_PREFLIGHT_OUTCOMES is 'held as one name so the CHECK above and the Python guard below can never drift into two different lists,' but the CHECK clause at ledger.py:67 is a separate hand-written literal inside the SCHEMA string, defined well before this tuple exists and never built from it. The two are two independent spellings of the same closed set, kept in sync only by hand — exactly the item-18 drift the comment claims is impossible. If a future change adds a third outcome to RUN_PREFLIGHT_OUTCOMES without also editing the SQL string in SCHEMA, set_run_preflight would accept the value in its Python guard and then fail with a sqlite3.IntegrityError on the UPDATE against any freshly created ledger, silently contradicting the comment's promise.
